etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English mechanical, mechanicalle, mechanycalle, equivalent to mechanic +‎ -al.

definitions.definition: (now rare) Characteristic of someone who does manual labour for a living; coarse, vulgar.

quote.citation: c. 1596–1599 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Second Part of Henry the Fourth, […]”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act V, scene v]:
quote.text: Thy Doll, and Helen of thy noble thoughts,Is in base durance and contagious prison,Haled thither by most mechanical and dirty hand.

quote.citation: 1603, Michel de Montaigne, chapter 43, in John Florio, transl., The Essayes […], book I, London:  […]  Val[entine] Simmes for Edward Blount […], →OCLC:
quote.text: all manner of silks were already become so vile and abject, that was any man seene to weare them, he was presently judged to be some countrie fellow, or mechanicall man.

definitions.definition: Related to mechanics (the branch of physics that deals with forces acting on mass).
Related to mechanics (the design and construction of machines).
Using mechanics (the design and construction of machines): being a machine.
(figurative) As if performed by a machine: lifeless, mindless, thoughtless, automatic.
(of a person) Acting as if one were a machine: lifeless or mindless.

quote.citation: 1918, W[illiam] B[abington] Maxwell, chapter XV, in The Mirror and the Lamp, Indianapolis, Ind.: The Bobbs-Merrill Company, →OCLC:
quote.text: Edward Churchill still attended to his work in a hopeless mechanical manner like a sleep-walker who walks safely on a well-known round. But his Roman collar galled him, his cossack stifled him, his biretta was as uncomfortable as a merry-andrew's cap and bells.

definitions.definition: (advertising) Manually created layout of artwork that is camera ready for photographic reproduction.

quote.citation: 1980, Henry C. Latimer, Production planning and repro mechanicals for offset printing, page 92:
quote.text: Since we are dealing with copy in paste-up form, we are now concerned with the preparation and assembly of elements suitable for camera-ready copy, positioned on the mechanical according to the rough layout supplied.

quote.citation: 1982, Jerry Demoney, Susan E. Meyer, Pasteups & mechanicals: a step-by-step guide to preparing art for reproduction:
quote.text: We'll start with a simple mechanical for a standard 7" x 10" ad, using one block of copy, some display type, and one picture.

quote.citation: 2009, New York State Sales and Use Tax Law and Regulations:
quote.text: In order to produce the posters, the advertising agency purchases photographs, composition and artwork and fabricates such property to produce layouts and mechanicals.

definitions.definition: One who does manual labor, especially one who is similar to Shakespeare's rude mechanicals

definitions.definition: (music) A stop on an organ that is operated by a hand or foot control rather than having to be manually set up in advance.

quote.citation: 1914, Expositor and Current Anecdotes - Volume 16, page 353:
quote.text: On the other hand I heard only recently of a modern marvel — an organ of two manuals and about sixteen or eighteen stops with adequate and modern mechanicals that the pastor assures me has not been touched by repairer or even by tuner in four years!

definitions.definition: (archaic) A machine that performs a job typically accomplished using an animal or manual labor.
